source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine - Engine Tune Up, p.6-10

procedures.title: Cranking voltage: test
steps: If the reading is 9 volts or more and cranking speed is good, the battery, starter, cables, starter switch and ignition circuit to the coil (bypassing the resistance wire) are all good.
If under 9 volts, trace the circuit until the fault is found.
notes: Low reading: weak battery; bad cables, connections, switch or starter; or faulty ignition circuit to coil.
Slow cranking: too much resistance in cables or starter, or excess mechanical drag in the engine.
Uneven cranking: uneven compression or a faulty starter or starter drive.

procedures.title: Ignition switch: test
steps: With the voltmeter hooked up as for the cranking voltage test, turn the ignition switch ON.
Voltage should fall to 5-7 volts, since current now flows through the resistance wire from the switch to the coil + terminal.
If full battery voltage (12 volts) shows, the starter solenoid is bypassing the resistance wire when it should not, or the circuit is wired wrong.

specs.what: coil + voltage, switch ON (engine not cranking)

procedures.title: Distributor resistance: test
steps: Test with the equipment per its maker's instructions.
Eliminate any excess primary resistance before going on.

procedures.title: Secondary resistance: test
steps: Test with the equipment per its maker's instructions.
Even normal readings mean all secondary parts are good.
All readings low: check for a corroded coil tower terminal, bad or broken coil wire, burned center cap electrode or rotor tip, or an open coil secondary.
High readings on 2 or more plugs next to each other in firing order: cross-firing in the cap or between those plug cables.
Meter off scale to the left: coil polarity reversed; check for swapped coil primary wires, wrong coil or reversed battery connections.

procedures.title: Ignition output and secondary leakage: test
steps: Test with the equipment per its maker's instructions.
GOOD readings mean ignition output and secondary insulation are both good.
All BAD, or the calibrator will not reach Set Line: check for high primary resistance or bad points, coil or condenser.
BAD only when certain plug wires are lifted: check the cap for cracks or carbon tracks and those wires for bad insulation.

procedures.title: Carburetor: additional adjustments
steps: Do adjustments such as idle vent, float level, pump rod and secondary valve per Section 6M.

procedures.title: Fuel pump: additional check
steps: If the owner reports poor high-speed performance, suspect the fuel pump.
